chapter: Harlem scene and race in music
title: New York as the center for pianists
summary: Fats Waller, J.P. Johnson and Willie the Lion show New York was the pianists' home.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, I don't know. The interesting thing about New York jazz, though, was look at the pianists that came from New York -- Fats Waller, J.P. Johnson, Willie 'the Lion' Smith, you know, from Newark, originally, but he really came up in New York, I think.
And this was really the center for the pianists.
Yeah. Well, a lot of times in jazz history, certain conceptions arise because they are early conceptions, and they go on and on and people don't
think of examining these older ideas. I'm not making any claim about the relative influence of New Orleans as against another place, but I think it's something worth discussing, as we have been.
